title: U.S. Treasury sells $58 billion of 3 or notes at a high yield of 4.474%
description: The 1st coupon auction of the week was met with average demand. The US treasury sold $58 billion of 3 or notes at a high yield of 4.474%. The WI level at the time of the auction was just above that level at 4.75% creating a tale of -0.1 basis points. Bid to cover 2.72X was higher than the average of 2.62X Domestic buyers (directs) took 26.9%, above the 20.4% average international buyers (indirects) took 64.2% versus 65.5% average Dealers took less than average at 10.9% vs 14.1% average.  This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

title: China August inflation seen rebounding as trade data flags demand gap
description: A rebound in headline CPI toward consensus would ease immediate deflation concerns without altering the broader policy picture, given the move is expected to be driven by a food price base effect rather than a genuine demand recovery. A miss, echoing July's shortfall against forecasts, would revive questions about the durability of domestic consumption and keep pressure on Beijing to lean further into stimulus.
